title: Consulting
text: Our team brings the experience of 65 published studies on drought, hydrology and climate change, and of projects funded by TÜBİTAK and universities, to organizations. We produce analyses and reports based on measured data, using the same methods we use in peer-reviewed work.

title: Consulting
text:
What we can work on


Drought risk
Meteorological and hydrological drought analysis for a province, basin or facility; drought severity, duration and return periods; drought risk maps.


Water resources and streamflow
Low- and high-flow analysis, low-flow frequency analysis, and hydrological inputs for water supply and environmental flow assessments.


Floods and extreme rainfall
Intensity-duration-frequency curves, trend analysis of extreme rainfall, and assessment of transitions between drought and flood.


Climate change impact
Future precipitation, temperature and drought conditions for a region or investment using CMIP6 scenarios; long-term trend analysis.


Agriculture and soil moisture
Agricultural drought monitoring with soil moisture and vegetation data, flash drought risk, and analyses for irrigation planning.


Data and forecasting models
Compiling and validating station, satellite and reanalysis data (MGM, ERA5-Land, GLEAM, CHIRPS); machine learning-based forecasting models.

title: Consulting
text:

Sector
Example need

title: Consulting
text:
What we deliver

Technical report: data, methods, findings and recommendations, ready for your decision process.
Maps and charts: drought risk maps, trend charts, return-period curves.
Data sets: cleaned and documented data used and produced in the analysis.
Presentations and training: presenting findings to your team; hands-on training on drought indices and trend analysis.
Joint projects: preparing and running joint proposals for TÜBİTAK, development agency and EU calls.

title: Consulting
text:
How we work

Initial meeting: we discuss your needs and the data you have.
Scope and proposal: we propose the method, deliverables and timeline in writing.
Analysis: we compile the data, run the analyses and share interim results with you.
Report and presentation: we deliver the results as a report and present them to your team.

title: Welcome to the Climate and Environment Group blog
text:
The Climate and Environment Group has launched its website and blog. We are researchers from several universities working on drought, climate change and water resources.
On this blog we will share:

New publications: short, non-technical summaries of what our papers found.
Projects: updates from our ongoing projects, such as the TÜBİTAK 1002-A flash drought project that started in August 2026.
Method notes: practical lessons from working with SPI/SPEI, copula analysis and innovative trend analysis (ITA, RW-ITA).
Events: congresses, seminars and announcements for students.

For questions or collaboration, please reach us via the Contact page.

title: Our work and the Sustainable Development Goals
text:
According to Scopus, our group’s work on drought, water resources and climate change is linked to the following United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):

Goal 6: Clean Water and Sanitation
Goal 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth
Goal 11: Sustainable Cities and Communities
Goal 13: Climate Action
Goal 14: Life Below Water
Goal 17: Partnerships for the Goals




Our team and the Sustainable Development Goals our work is linked to


Our studies measure drought risk, changes in streamflow and the impacts of climate change. We aim for them to support decision makers in areas ranging from water resources management to climate adaptation in cities.

title: Methods
text:
SPI (Standardized Precipitation Index) and SPEI (Standardized Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index). We track precipitation deficits and the effect of temperature at different time scales (e.g. 3, 6 and 12 months), and use rolling-window SPI/SPEI to study how drought regimes change.



We identify drought at streamflow gauging stations with the SDI (Streamflow Drought Index) and study low and high flows and transitions between drought and flood.



We detect flash droughts that develop within weeks using soil moisture data, validate them with the SPEI, and assess their effects on vegetation.

text:

We detect flash droughts that develop within weeks using soil moisture data, validate them with the SPEI, and assess their effects on vegetation.

title: Methods
text:
Drought events and frequency analysis
We describe each drought event by its duration, severity, intensity and peak. Because duration and severity are linked, we use copula functions for bivariate frequency analysis and compute univariate, bivariate and conditional return periods. From these we produce basin-scale drought risk maps.

title: Methods
text:
Trend and change analysis







Method
What we use it for




Mann-Kendall and Spearman’s rho
Statistical significance of a trend


Sen’s slope
Magnitude of a trend (units per year)


Innovative trend analysis (ITA, IPTA)
Separate trends in low, medium and high values


Rolling-window ITA (RW-ITA)
Detecting hidden trends whose direction changes over time


Homogeneity and change-point tests
Finding breaks and abrupt shifts in a series



RW-ITA was developed by our group: Eşit et al. (2026), Water Resources Management.

title: Methods
text:
Machine learning and forecasting
We use artificial neural networks, deep learning and feature selection to estimate climate parameters and drought indices. We also work on seasonal to multi-year forecasting of soil moisture drought.

Drought · Climate Change · Water Resources
Climate and Environment Group
We are a multi-university research group working on drought, climate change and water resources using station and gridded data.
Our projects Publications

title: Climate and Environment Group
text:
Research areas


Drought analysis
SPI and SPEI indices, drought event duration, severity and intensity, multivariate (copula) frequency analysis.


Trends and variability
Trend detection in precipitation, temperature and streamflow series with Mann-Kendall, Sen’s slope, innovative trend analysis (ITA, IPTA) and rolling-window RW-ITA.


Climate projections
Regional assessments using CMIP6 scenarios, ERA5 reanalysis and CHIRPS precipitation.


Soil moisture and streamflow
Flash drought, soil moisture and vegetation response; low/high flows and drought–flood transitions.

title: Climate and Environment Group

Consulting for organizations
We prepare drought risk, streamflow and extreme rainfall analyses and climate change impact reports for municipalities, water utilities, and agriculture, energy and insurance companies.
